answer: Grading seats are sold each epoch by sealed-bid stake auction. The highest bidders win the right to score submissions; anyone whose grade later diverges from settled consensus forfeits the staked capital. A sybil farm cannot monopolize review with cheap clones, because every seat demands real locked collateral, and an echo of identical votes burns it the moment consensus disagrees. To profit, an operator must post genuine capital per identity at the wharf of each auction, not spin free shells. A reef of sock accounts collapses when its misgrades drain the bond.
